whatItIs.text: Oil pressed from sesame seeds — among the earliest-known crop oils; the untoasted kind cooks, the toasted kind perfumes dishes at the end.

historyNote.text: Sesame capsules burst only when fully ripe, so harvest stays stubbornly manual — one reason world production is just 1.2 million tonnes (2023), led by India and Myanmar. Toasted sesame oil is a finishing oil: frying it burns the toasted flavour bitter.

howToChoose.text: For Asian cooking buy toasted (dark, fragrant); for general frying, the light raw-seed oil. Dark glass bottles protect the aroma from light.

storage.text: Keep cool and dark; sesame oil is one of the more stable natural oils but still resents light and heat — the fridge preserves it longest.

useItUp.text: A few drops fix almost any bland noodle, soup, or dipping sauce; mix stale-ish oil into dressings where toasting flavour matters less than freshness.
